summary: Tank is once more hunched over the monitors, hunting through the Matrix, when the PHONE RINGS. He answers it by saying "Operator." A voice identified as Cypher (V.O.) demands "I need an exit! Fast!" Tank recognizes the caller, responding with the single word "Cypher?"

what_changes.before: Alone at the monitors searching the Matrix, unaware of who is calling
what_changes.after: Learns through the phone that the caller is Cypher, who urgently needs an exit

event_hint.one_line: Cypher calls the Nebuchadnezzar demanding a fast exit, and Tank recognizes him as the caller.

minds.wants: To identify the caller and respond correctly as operator, staying ready to execute an exit.
minds.feels: He is still reeling from Morpheus's capture (sc-124's "No!"), so his whole nervous system is primed for crisis — and the last person he expects to hear from, Cypher, is the one on the line. His single-word reply carries the shock of a man who has just been handed something that does not fit.
minds.shows: A flat, procedural "Operator," then a bare, questioning "Cypher?" — he names the caller rather than acting on the exit request, which lets us see that recognition has momentarily overridden his operator's reflex.
minds.basis: He answers with the rote "Operator," then, instead of confirming the exit, responds only with the name "Cypher?" — a break in procedure that marks surprise. This follows sc-124, where he was just watching Morpheus taken and crying out in helplessness.

believes_about.belief: Cypher is a fellow crew member who is out in the Matrix and in trouble, needing a real extraction — a comrade calling for help.
believes_about.wrong_because: The event shape establishes that Cypher has already betrayed the crew: he unplugged, killed Dozer, shot Tank, and killed Apoc and Switch. Tank's assumption that this is a legitimate rescue call is exactly the trap Cypher is laying.

minds.wants: To get Tank to open an exit line fast, before anyone on the ship realizes what he has done.
minds.feels: Urgency and calculation — he is running a con against the clock, needing to sound like a desperate man being chased so that Tank does not stop to ask the questions that would expose him.
minds.shows: Only a clipped, anonymous demand — "I need an exit! Fast!" — that withholds his identity entirely, forcing Tank to supply it. He lets be seen a man under pressure; he conceals that he is the one who created the pressure.
minds.basis: He opens with a demand for a fast exit rather than identifying himself, and it is Tank who names him — meaning Cypher deliberately avoided giving his name, consistent with a betrayer who must keep Tank off-balance. The event confirms he has just murdered crewmates and is now manipulating the ship from outside.

believes_about.belief: Tank is still just an operator at his post, unaware that Cypher has already killed Dozer, shot him, and killed Apoc and Switch — so he can be played with a fake distress call.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is Cypher's operative assumption driving the call; whether it holds depends on what Tank has learned since sc-124, which this scene does not show. Cypher is betting the crew's attention is still on Morpheus's capture, not on him.

connects_back: sc-124: Tank's helpless "No!" at Morpheus's capture leaves him at the monitors in a heightened, crisis-ready state when this call arrives.
sc-125: Trinity has just surfaced, so the crew is mid-extraction and expecting to pull people out — the frame within which Cypher's fake distress call lands.
ev-023: Cypher has already betrayed the crew (killed Dozer, shot Tank, killed Apoc and Switch), which is the hidden reality this call is built on top of.
sets_up: ev-023: Cypher's demand for a fast exit is the mechanism by which he intends to complete his betrayal — getting himself reinserted while the crew believes he is in danger.
ev-024: The crew's debate over Morpheus's fate and the fallout of the betrayal follows from this moment of Cypher contacting the ship under false pretenses.
The recognition beat ("Cypher?") sets up the crew's dawning realization that the caller is not a man to be rescued but the traitor among them.
dramatic_function: This is the betrayal beginning to surface in the open: it converts Cypher's off-screen treachery into a live, ticking interaction and places Tank — still grieving Morpheus — at the exact point where he must recognize the enemy he does not yet know to fear, turning a routine operator exchange into the first crack of the trap closing.
